subject: Post-call recap: capacity needs, burst patterns & overage terms for Acme Payments
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: capacity needs, burst patterns & overage terms for Acme Payments

Hi Alicia — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before procurement jumps in.

Summary of what I captured from the call:
- Baseline monthly tokens: ~1.2 billion tokens/month (inference tokens, not input-only).
- Planned marketing push (May) could create sustained uplift to ~2.6–3.0B tokens/month for 6–8 weeks.
- Short spikes during campaign launches: ~8–10x baseline QPS for 5–15 minutes; more common is 3–4x for 10–30 minutes.
- Target unit economics mentioned on the call: you flagged a budget range around $350–$650 per 1M tokens (you said procurement prefers < $450 if possible).

Open questions / asks for you:
1) Can you confirm the month-to-month variability window (is May the only heavy month or do you expect recurring campaigns)?
2) Is Acme comfortable with a Hosted (pay-as-you-go) deployment to start, or are you evaluating a Dedicated reserved capacity commitment? (Committed capacity reduces unit $/1M considerably.)
3) Procurement asked for a clear overage policy: hard caps, burst allowance, and invoice math. I can send a compact worked example and the commit vs hosted comparison.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send a short pricing summary with three scenarios (Hosted PAYG, 12-month Dedicated commit, and Hybrid with burst buffer) by EOD PT tomorrow.
- If procurement wants, we can set a 30-minute pricing deep-dive early next week (I’ll include RevOps).

Attaching the initial pricing estimate I referenced on the call (redwood-pricing-estimate-v1.pdf).

Thanks — talk soon.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: capacity needs, burst patterns & overage terms for Acme Payments

Thanks Priyom — that summary looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- Volume profile: May is the biggest run, but we also run smaller promos in Aug/Nov that produce ~2x baseline for a week. So yes, variability is recurring but with a single big peak.
- Procurement’s ask: please show a concrete invoice example for overage charges (they want to avoid surprise invoices). Also include whether you support a hard spend cap or automatic throttling when a quota is reached.
- Target $/1M tokens: we would be pushing hard for ~$400 per 1M tokens net (that’s the aspiration for this procurement). If that’s only possible with a commit, be explicit about the commit size and term required.

One more: for short bursts (under 30 minutes) we want to know the per-minute QPS you can sustain without switching to overage pricing. Procurement wants a SLA-friendly statement we can put in the SOW.

If you can send an example invoice and an explicit burst/overage policy, procurement will be much happier. I’ve CC’d procurement so they see the thread.

— Alicia
Alicia Moreno
VP of Engineering, Acme Payments
alicia.moreno@acmepayments.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: capacity needs, burst patterns & overage terms for Acme Payments

Alicia — thanks, that helps. Below is a concise worked example plus our standard burst/overage policy and the options that get you toward the $400/1M target. I’ll also upload the revised commit options spreadsheet (attached).

Quick pricing primer (rounded numbers for clarity):
- Hosted (PAYG): $600 per 1M tokens baseline. No upfront commit.
  - Short burst allowance: we permit up to 3x your steady quota for 10 continuous minutes without triggering overage billing (designed for quick campaign ramps).
  - Overage beyond allowed burst window: charged at 1.5x baseline (i.e., $900 per 1M tokens).
  - Hard spend cap: supported — we can enforce an account-level hard cap that blocks requests once reached (recommended if you want invoice certainty).

- Dedicated (12-month reserved capacity example): $420 per 1M tokens with a 12-month commit of 1.5B tokens/month (discounts scale up for larger commits).
  - Burst buffer: reserved pools include a configurable burst pool; overage pricing for short burst above reserved capacity is billed at 1.1x committed rate for the month it happens.
  - If you need sustained extra capacity beyond the reserve, we can provision temporary additional nodes (lead time 24–72h) billed at on-demand rates.

Worked invoice example (baseline month without big campaign):
- Committed Dedicate plan at $420/1M tokens; usage = 1.2B tokens -> invoice = (1,200 * $420) = $504,000

Worked invoice example (campaign month with 2.8B tokens used; 1.5B committed):
- Committed portion invoice: 1,500 * $420 = $630,000
- Excess tokens: 1,300 * $462 (1.1x committed overage) = $600,600
- Total = $1,230,600

Worked invoice example Hosted PAYG with overage (no commit):
- Baseline 1.2B tokens at $600/1M = $720,000
- Campaign month usage 2.8B tokens total -> excess 1.6B * $900 (1.5x overage) = $1,440,000
- Total = $2,160,000

What it takes to reach the ~$400/1M target you mentioned:
- A $400/1M net requires a multi-month commit and a larger minimum commitment than you described on the call. Rough breakpoint: 24-month commitment at ~3B tokens/month or a mix of a 12-month commit + guaranteed growth staircase. I put a couple of modeled options in the attached spreadsheet (redwood-revised-commit-options.xlsx).

Burst details (SLA-friendly):
- Short bursts: up to 3x steady quota sustained for 10 minutes without overage billing; automatic fallback applies to protect latency SLOs.
- Extended bursts: >10 continuous minutes at >3x quota will consume burst allowance and then count as overage on a minute-by-minute basis.
- Rate limiting: configurable per-customer QPS ceiling; we can set an emergency throttle that kicks in at your chosen spend threshold.

Next steps I recommend:
1) If procurement wants a deterministic invoice, pick between: a) Dedicated 12/24-month commit (I’ll send exact pricing tiers), or b) Hosted + hard spend cap + pre-approved overage multiplier.
2) Schedule the 30-minute pricing session — I’ll invite RevOps and our pricing lead so we can agree on commit sizing and legal SOW language.
3) I’ll add the worked invoice examples and a short SOW-friendly burst clause to the HubSpot record and share a DocuSign MSA draft if you want to accelerate.

Attachment: redwood-revised-commit-options.xlsx (Excel, 2 tabs)

Let me know a couple of times that work for the deep-dive next week.

— Priyom
